top: A wide shot of someone doing the task.
bottom: A tight, lit close-up of the single most interesting detail.
caption:
Your B-roll is boring because you film the action, not the detail.

Wide and busy = filler.
Close, lit, and isolated = intentional.

Get uncomfortably close to the most interesting thing in the frame.

headline: What makes an edit feel 'fast' (it's not talking fast).
bullets: Cut the breath before every sentence
Land captions on the beat, not after
Switch the frame every couple lines
Trim anything that isn't the point
footer_note: Pace is edited in, not talked in.
caption:
A video feels fast because of the edit, not because you talk fast.

1. Cut the breath before each sentence
2. Land captions on the beat
3. Switch the frame every couple lines
4. Trim anything that isn't the point

Pace is something you build in the timeline.

Follow @josephborroto for editing that holds attention.

#videoediting #editingtips #pacing #shortformvideo #reelstips #josephborroto

headline: The 3-part hook formula you can reuse forever.
bullets: Call out exactly who it's for
Name the problem they feel
Promise the payoff in one line
footer_note: Works in any niche. Save it.
caption:
Steal this hook formula and reuse it forever:

1. Call out who it's for — "If you run a local business..."
2. Name the problem — "...your Reels are getting ignored"
3. Promise the payoff — "...here's the 1 fix"

Three lines. Endless variations. Save it.

Follow @josephborroto for frameworks you can actually use.

headline: That's all your hook gets.
subheadline: Make the first line impossible to scroll past.
caption:

Most people waste it on "hey guys, in this video..." By the time they get to the point, the viewer's gone.

Lead with the problem. Earn the next second.

headline: Statement hooks beat question hooks.
